@@133943007 <h> How the Cotswolds Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty came about <p> One of Mark Connelly 's favourite Cotswold locations are the valleys around Bath ( Image : Mark Connelly ) <p> This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today , and has been written by our American colleagues . It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald . <p> Our mellow limestone towns and villages , dramatic western escarpment and high-wolds views are rightly world famous , encapsulating for many people a quintessence of rural England . Sixty years ago , in 1966 , official steps were taken to safeguard this distinctive allure for the nation 's benefit , through designation of the Cotswolds as an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty ( AONB ) -- an anniversary that we will be celebrating throughout 2026 . <p> Extended in area in 1990 , rebranded as a National Landscape in 2020 , and covering 787sq miles ( 2,038sq km ) , the Cotswolds is the largest National Landscape in the UK and rich with scenic diversity . Yet -- and @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ a special landscape -- it has a remarkable visual harmony , all thanks to the underlying geology of its Jurassic limestone . <p> Used in the building of towns and villages , as well as farmland networks of dry-stone walls , the limestone organically shade-shifts from warm honey tones in the northern Cotswolds to greys around Stroud and pale creams around Bath . Limestone grasslands fed the sheep that brought huge wealth to the area in medieval times , leaving behind a legacy of ' wool ' churches and manor houses . Our internationally important beechwoods -- fiery orange icons of autumn -- thrive on limestone soils , and around half the country 's rare , bright-speckled , flower-rich Jurassic limestone grassland survives right here in the Cotswolds . <p> While an instinctive popular image of the Cotswolds is embedded deep in the national psyche , designation as an AONB ' has subsequently helped people to pin things down in defining exactly what landscape characteristics make it distinctive , ' says Mark Connelly , Land Management Lead for Cotswolds National Landscape ( CNL ) . As well as the unifying @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ ancient broadleaved woodlands and flower-rich grasslands , there 's away-from-it-all tranquillity and dark sky areas ideal for stargazing . <p> Designation comes with the statutory purpose ' to conserve and enhance ' the landscape 's natural beauty , and the CNL team has an additional statutory purpose to increase ' understanding and enjoyment ' of its special qualities . However , ' AONBs -- National Landscapes -- are n't preserved in aspic , ' Mark is quick to point out . ' Landscapes have always changed and always will , and it is about managing that change in a way that conserves and enhances the natural beauty and special qualities . ' <p> Farming is a crucial case in point . ' The Cotswolds landscape is a product of farming and if we are going to conserve and enhance the landscape , we need farming to continue to be viable , ' Mark says . Successful CNL collaborations over the years have ranged from the Cotswold Farmland Bird Project to reverse the decline in species numbers , to the delivery of the government 's Farming in Protected Landscapes ( FiPL @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ ) . FiPL has boosted local farm businesses with over ? 5 million funding towards nature , climate , people , and place projects , and supported farmers on their journey to adopt holistic , regenerative agriculture practices . <p> ' The Cotswolds is a real hotspot for learning about regenerative agriculture , partly because the soils lend themselves to it and also because there is a brilliant community of farmers , ' Mark says . <p> Another standout project is CNL 's work to nurture and extend the Cotswolds ' precious wildflower-rich limestone grasslands , initiating the restoration of nearly 500 hectares of land through its Glorious Cotswold Grasslands work from 2019 ? to 2025 alone . ' The Cotswolds is uniquely placed to restore and create these important grasslands ; it is one of our USPs when it comes to nature recovery , ' Mark says . <p> These and further landscape activities will be celebrated in future issues of Cotswold Life , as well as exploring how we can all help to make the Cotswolds resilient against climate change . <p> ' If we came back in @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ landscape is different , ' Mark says . ' But if it still feels and looks like the Cotswolds , then designation has been successful . ' <p> The picturesque towns and villages of the Cotswolds attract visitors all year . ( Image : Tea Smart ) <p> UNDERSTAND &amp; ENJOY <p> In fulfilling its brief to promote understanding and enjoyment of the Cotswolds , the CNL team has carried out lots of work to create and extend walking and cycling routes : from its Cotswold Gateways project to encourage more people to explore the countryside on their doorstep around towns and villages , to partnership working throughout the recent Bathscape Access Project featuring the Circuit of Bath and 19 self-guided walking routes to suit diverse abilities and interests , also encouraging mental wellbeing . <p> There has been a focus , too , on making routes accessible to people with mobility issues , with Removing Barriers funds used to support the purchase of Tramper mobility vehicles for use at sites across the Cotswolds . <p> ' Getting more people out into the countryside has always been an aim but @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ everybody should have access to nature , ' says Rebecca Jones MBE , CNL 's Access and Volunteers Lead . <p> Rebecca is quick to commend the array of people , from wildlife trusts to parish councils and community groups , that partner with CNL in making things happen . The Cotswold Voluntary Wardens put in a record-breaking 55,352 hours of work in 2025 -- 2025 alone , improving paths , stiles and gates , planting trees and hedges , and leading guided walks . Their outreach work has included helping to engage young people with river habitats through the Everyone 's Evenlode Project ( Cotswold Life , October 2025 issue ) . <p> Established in the late 1960s , the Cotswold Voluntary Wardens ' are amazing , ' Rebecca says . ' They now number more than 400 , and they come from all walks of life , bringing different skills , enthusiasm , knowledge and passion for the area . Hopefully during CNL 's 60th anniversary year even more people will be interested to get involved as volunteers , continuing to make the Cotswolds welcoming to everybody . @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ offering a series of special CNL60-themed guided walks . A fascinating feature-length documentary Cotswolds : Field &amp; Folk will be launched and toured , eavesdropping on local farmers and people who look after the landscape . Watch this space for more anniversary activities to be announced in coming months . <p> TIME-OUT TIPS <p> Both Mark and Rebecca have worked for the National Landscape for more than 30 years . Where do they like to take time out ? <p> Mark : ' I really like walking the enclosed limestone valleys around Bath , which are fascinating as landforms -- misfit valleys scoured out by ice melt . You also come across unexpected views , grasslands , ancient woodlands , and industrial archaeology . ' <p> Rebecca : ' I love ancient woodlands , like Lineover Wood near Dowdeswell where there 's a thousand-year-old beechwood tree . It 's beautiful there and you get a wonderful sense of history . ' <p> SPECIAL RESPONSIBILITIES <p> The Cotswolds National Landscape Board has two statutory purposes : <p> * to conserve and enhance the natural beauty of the Cotswolds National Landscape <p> @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ . <p> The Board also has a duty to foster the economic and social wellbeing of those who live here , cotswolds-nl.org.uk <h> Useful Links <p> This website and associated newspapers adhere to the Independent Press Standards Organisation 's Editors ' Code of Practice . Prof Alice Wiseman , director of public health for Newcastle and Gateshead , has called for urgent action to create a fairer system where everyone has the right to affordable and nutritious food -- instead of being forced to skip meals or rely on cheaper , unhealthy products . <p> ? <p> In a report presented to Newcastle City Council last week , she warns that food inequality is driving " unmanageable healthcare demands on the NHS " , leaving people with problems ranging from chronic stress and isolation to malnutrition , tooth decay to heart disease .
